definitions.gloss: to become used to using; to get accustomed to
definitions.explanation: to become familiar and comfortable with using something through repeated use

examples.japanese: この{包丁|ほうちょう}に{使|つか}い{慣|な}れている。
examples.english: I'm used to using this kitchen knife.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいパソコンに{使|つか}い{慣|な}れるまで{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took time to get used to the new computer.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}い{慣|な}れた{道具|どうぐ}は{手放|てばな}せない。
examples.english: I can't part with tools I've grown accustomed to using.

notes:
{使|つか}い{慣|な}れる means to become comfortable using something through experience.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {使|つか}い{慣|な}れている (have become used to using)
- {使|つか}い{慣|な}れた～ (～ that one is used to using)
- ～に{使|つか}い{慣|な}れる (to get used to using ～)
- {使|つか}い{慣|な}れた{道具|どうぐ} (tools one is used to)
- {使|つか}い{慣|な}れた{言葉|ことば} (words one is used to using)
- ～に{使|つか}い{慣|な}れるまで (until getting used to ~)

USAGE:
- Emphasizes familiarity and comfort from repeated use
- Often used when comparing old familiar items with new ones
- Implies efficiency and ease that comes with experience

RELATED WORDS:
- {使|つか}い{込|こ}む (to become skilled at using, to embezzle)
- {慣|な}れる (to get used to - general)
- {手慣|てな}れた (accustomed, skilled)

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive in the sense of becoming accustomed.

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in everyday speech.
